title: CHAPTER 2 : BASIC CONCEPTS OF Logic
content:
👋 ሰላም ውድ የEthioFresh ተማሪዎች! እንኳን ወደ Chapter 2 በሰላም መጣችሁ! የLogic ኮርስ ለMid Exam ከፍተኛ ነጥብ የሚይዝ፣ ለአስተሳሰብ ጥራትና ለሕይወትም በጣም ወሳኝ የሆነ ትምህርት ነው። የመጀመሪያ ዓመት (Freshman) ተማሪዎቻችን በፈተና 100% ሙሉ ነጥብ እንድታመጡና ይዘቱን በቀላሉ እንድትረዱት አድርገን በEthioFresh Standard Layout አዘጋጅተነዋል። ዘና እያላችሁ በጥራት ተማሩ! 🚀😄👇👇👇


Chapter Overview: Basic Concepts of Logic

• Logic, as a field of study, may be defined as the organized body of knowledge, or science, that evaluates arguments. The primary aim of logic is to develop a system of methods and principles that we may use as criteria for evaluating the arguments of others and as guides in constructing arguments of our own.
• An argument is a systematic combination of two or more statements, which are classified as a premise (or premises) and a conclusion. A premise refers to the statement which is claimed to provide logical support or evidence to the main point of the argument, known as the conclusion. A conclusion is a statement which is claimed to follow from the alleged evidence.
• Depending on the logical and real ability of the premise(s) to support the conclusion, an argument can be either a good argument or a bad argument. However, unlike all kinds of passages, including those that resemble arguments, all arguments purport to prove something.

👉 Chapter Overview ፡
• ሎጂክ (Logic) ማለት የተከራካሪዎችን መዋቅር እና ማስረጃ የምንመዝንበት የተደራጀ የዕውቀት ዘርፍ ወይም ሳይንስ ነው። የሎጂክ ዋና ዓላማ የሌሎችን ክርክር ትክክለኛነት የምንመዝንበትንና የራሳችንን ጠንካራ ክርክር የምንገነባበትን ደንቦች ማወቅ ነው።
• ማንኛውም Argument (ክርክር) ከሁለት ወይም ከዛ በላይ አረፍተ ነገሮች (Statements) ይመሰረታል፡
- Premise (መነሻ ማስረጃ)፡ ለዋናው ሀሳብ እንደ ማስረጃ ወይም ድጋፍ ሆኖ የሚያገለግል አረፍተ ነገር ነው።
- Conclusion (መደምደሚያ)፡ ከቀረበው ማስረጃ ተነስቶ የሚደረስበት ዋና ነጥብ ነው።
• 💡 በዕለት ተዕለት ውይይት የምናደርገው ተራ ጭቅጭቅ በሎጂክ ትርጉም "Argument" አይባልም! በሎጂክ Argument የሚባለው ማስረጃ የቀረበለት እና መደምደሚያ ያለው ሀሳብ ብቻ ነው።


Deductive and Inductive Arguments Overview

• Arguments can generally be divided into deductive and inductive arguments.
• Deductive Argument: An argument in which the premises are claimed to support the conclusion in such a way that it is impossible for the premises to be true and the conclusion false. Evaluated by its validity and soundness. A valid deductive argument can be either sound or unsound depending on its factual claim.
• Inductive Argument: An argument in which the premises are claimed to support the conclusion in such a way that it is improbable that the premises be true and the conclusion false. Evaluated by its strength and cogency. If strong and all premises are actually true, it is cogent; otherwise, uncogent.

👉 Deductive vs Inductive ፡
• አርጉመንቶች በሁለት ዋና ዋና ክፍሎች ይከፈላሉ፡
1. Deductive Argument: ማስረጃዎቹ (Premises) እውነት ከሆኑ መደምደሚያው (Conclusion) በምንም ተአምር ሐሰት ሊሆን አይችልም (100% እርግጠኝነት አለ)።
• Evaluation: Valid/Invalid እና Sound/Unsound ተብሎ ይገመገማል።
2. Inductive Argument: ማስረጃዎቹ እውነት ሲሆኑ መደምደሚያው እውነት የመሆን እድሉ ከፍተኛ ነው (Probability/ግምት እንጂ 100% እርግጠኝነት የለውም)።
• Evaluation: Strong/Weak እና Cogent/Uncogent ተብሎ ይገመገማል።


1. What is the Meaning of Logic?

• The word logic comes from the Greek word logos, which means sentence, discourse, reason, truth, and rule. Logic in its broader meaning is the science that evaluates arguments and the study of correct reasoning. It could also be defined as the study of methods and principles of correct reasoning or the art of correct reasoning.
• Specific definitions of logic include:
- Logic is a science that evaluates arguments.
- Logic is the study of methods for evaluating arguments (specifically whether premises adequately support conclusions).
- Logic helps to develop the methods and principles used as criteria for evaluating others' arguments and constructing good arguments of our own.
- Logic is the attempt to codify the rules of rational thought.
- Logic is one of the primary tools philosophers use to cope with the subtlety of philosophical problems and the often misleading nature of conversational language.
• In logic, as an academic discipline, we study reasoning itself: forms of argument, general principles, and particular errors, along with methods of arguing. Logic helps us understand what is wrong in daily life mistakes in reasoning or why someone is arguing in a particular way.

👉 የLogic ትርጉም ፡
• Logic የሚለው ቃል የመጣው Logos ከተባለ የግሪክ ቃል ሲሆን ትርጉሙም ሀሳብ፣ ንግግር፣ ምክንያት፣ እውነት ወይም ህግ ማለት ነው።
• በአጭሩ ሎጂክ ማለት፡
1. የሰዎችን ክርክርና ማስረጃ ትክክለኛነት የምንመዝንበት ሳይንስ ነው።
2. ትክክለኛ የአስተሳሰብና የምክንያታዊነት ስልቶችን (Correct Reasoning) የምንማርበት መስክ ነው።
3. ሰዎች በንግግርና በቋንቋ ውዥንብር ውስጥ እንዳያስታሉን የሚከላከል መከላከያ ጋሻችን ነው!

What is the Benefit of Studying Logic?
• "Logic sharpens and refines our natural gifts to think, reason and argue." — C. S. Layman
• We all think, reason, and argue in day-to-day communications. While the ability to reason may partially be a natural gift, logic refines, improves, and sharpens this ability.
• Major benefits include:
- Helps construct sound (good) and fallacy-free arguments of one's own and evaluate those of others.
- Provides a fundamental defense against prejudiced and uncivilized attitudes that threaten a civilized and democratic society.
- Helps distinguish good arguments from bad arguments.
- Helps understand and identify common logical errors in reasoning.
- Helps identify common confusions arising from the misuse of language.
- Enables us to disclose ill-conceived policies in the political sphere and distinguish rational from irrational thought.

👉 የLogic ጥቅም ፡
• የተሳሳቱ አመለካከቶችን (Fallacies) ለመለየት፡ በካምፓስም ሆነ በውጭ ህይወት ሰዎች በስሜት ወይም በተሳሳተ መረጃ እንዳያታልሉን ይረዳል።
• ዲሞክራሲያዊ አእምሮን ለመገንባት፡ ከስሜታዊነትና ሚዛናዊ ካልሆነ (Prejudice) ይልቅ በምክንያት እንድንነጋገር ያደርጋል።
• ፖሊሲዎችንና የፖለቲካ ንግግሮችን ለመገምገም፡ የፖሊሲ አውጪዎችን ባዶ ፕሮፓጋንዳ ከእውነተኛ ምክንያታዊ መረጃ ለመለየት ያግዛል።

💡 Exam Hint :
• ፈተና ላይ "Which of the following is NOT a benefit of studying logic?" ተብሎ ሊመጣ ይችላል።
• ሎጂክ ተፈጥሮአዊ የማሰብ ችሎታችንን አዲስ የሚፈጥር ሳይሆን የሚቀርጽና የሚያድስ (refines, improves and sharpens) መሆኑን አትርሱ!


2. What is an Argument?

• In logic, an argument is defined as a technical term referring to a group of statements, one or more of which (the premises) are claimed to provide support for, or reason to believe, one of the other (the conclusion).
• It does NOT mean a mere verbal fight or dispute with friends, parents, or spouses.
• Key Requirements:
1. Must be a group of statements.
2. Must contain at least one premise and one and only one conclusion.

👉 Argument ማለት ምን ማለት ነው? ፡
• የአረፍተ ነገሮች ስብስብ ሆኖ፣ ቢያንስ አንድ Premise (ማስረጃ) እና አንድ የጋራ Conclusion (መደምደሚያ) ያለው የሀሳብ መዋቅር ነው።
• 🚨 ወርቃማ ህግ: አንድ አርጉመንት ውስጥ ከ1 በላይ Premise ሊኖር ይችላል፤ ነገር ግን Conclusion ሁልጊዜም ቢሆን Exactly 1 (አንድ ብቻ) ነው!

A. What is a Statement?
• A statement is a declarative sentence that has a truth-value of either true or false. Truth and falsity are the two possible truth-values of a statement.
• Examples:
a) Dr. Abiy Ahmed is the current Prime Minister of Ethiopia (True).
b) Mekelle is the capital city of Tigray Region (True).
c) Ethiopia was colonized by Germany (False).
• N.B: Logicians use "proposition" and "statement" interchangeably. Strictly, a proposition is the meaning or information content of a statement.
• Non-Statements: Sentences that are NOT statements cannot be used to construct an argument:
a) Questions: "Would you close the window?"
b) Proposals: "Let us study together."
c) Exclamations: "Right on!"
d) Suggestions: "I suggest that you read philosophy texts."
e) Commands: "Give me your ID Card, Now!"
• None of these non-statements have truth-values (they are neither true nor false), so none can form an argument.

👉 Statement እና Non-Statement ፡
• አንድ አረፍተ ነገር Statement ለመባል እውነት (True) ወይም ሐሰት (False) ልንለው የምንችል (Declarative) መሆን አለበት።
• ❌ ለፈተና ያዙ፡ Questions, Commands, Proposals, Suggestions, እና Exclamations Truth-Value (እውነት/ሐሰት የመባል ባህሪ) ስለሌላቸው Statement አይደሉም፤ Argument መገንባት አይችሉም!

B. Premises and Conclusion
• Premise: A statement that sets forth the reason or evidence given for accepting the conclusion of an argument.
• Conclusion: A statement claimed to follow from the given evidence (premise). It is the main claim that an argument is trying to establish.
• Example 1 (Good Argument):
1) All Ethiopians are Africans. (Premise 1)
2) Tsionawit is Ethiopian. (Premise 2)
Therefore, Tsionawit is African. (Conclusion)
• Example 2 (Bad Argument):
1) Some Africans are black. (Premise 1)
2) Zelalem is an African. (Premise 2)
Therefore, Zelalem is black. (Conclusion)
• In both examples, the first two statements are premises, and the third is the conclusion. Example 1 is good because premises support the conclusion; Example 2 is bad because premises fail to adequately support the conclusion, but it is still an argument.

• Premise (መነሻ ማስረጃ/ምክንያት): Provides Support/Evidence for the argument.
• Conclusion (ዋና መደምደሚያ ሀሳብ): Main Claim of the argument (Must be Exactly 1).


3. Techniques of Identifying Premises and Conclusions

• Distinguishing premises from conclusions is one of the most important tasks in logic. Identifying indicator words is the first technique used.

A. Conclusion Indicators ፡
• Words that indicate the conclusion follows: Therefore, Wherefore, Accordingly, Provided that, It must be that, We may conclude, Entails that, Hence, It shows that, Whence, Thus, Consequently, We may infer, It implies that, As a result, So, It follows that.
• Example: Women are mammals. Zenebech is a woman. Therefore, Zenebech is a mammal. ("Zenebech is a mammal" is the conclusion following "therefore").

B. Premise Indicators ፡
• Words that indicate a premise follows: Since, As indicated by, Because, Owing to, Seeing that, Given that, As, For, In that, May be inferred from, Inasmuch as, For the reason that.
• Example: You should avoid any form of cheating on exams because cheating on exams is punishable by the Senate Legislation of the University. ("cheating on exams is punishable..." is the premise following "because").

C. Special Case: "For this reason" ፡
• "For this reason" comes immediately after the premise it indicates and before the conclusion.
• Structure: [Premise] + for this reason + [Conclusion]
• Do not confuse "for this reason" with "for the reason that" (which introduces a premise).
• Single indicators can also introduce multiple premises. Example: "Tsionawit is a faithful wife, for Ethiopian women are faithful wives and Tsionawit is an Ethiopian." ("for" introduces both premises).

D. Arguments Without Indicators & Non-Premise Elements ፡
• When no indicators exist, ask these questions to find the conclusion:
- What single statement is claimed (implicitly) to follow from the others?
- What is the arguer trying to prove?
- What is the main point in the passage?
• Example: "Our country should increase the quality and quantity of its military. Ethnic conflicts are recently intensified; border conflicts are escalating; international terrorist activities are increasing."
- Main point / Conclusion: "Our country should increase the quality and quantity of its military."
- Premises: Ethnic conflicts, border conflicts, terrorist activities.
• Passing Comments: Passages may contain statements that are neither premises nor conclusions (passing comments). They should be excluded.
• Inference: In a narrower sense, it means the reasoning process expressed by the argument. Broadly, it refers to the argument itself.

👉 Indicator Words እና ልዩ ሁኔታዎች ፡
• Conclusion Indicators: ከእነሱ ቀጥሎ የሚመጣው ሀሳብ Conclusion ነው።
• Premise Indicators: ከእነሱ ቀጥሎ የሚመጣው ሀሳብ Premise ነው።
• "For this reason" ልዩ ሁኔታ: ከቃሉ በፊት ያለው Premise ሲሆን፣ ከቃሉ በኋላ ያለው Conclusion ነው! (ከ "for the reason that" ጋር እንዳታደባልቁት)።
• Passing Comments: ከአርጉመንቱ ጋር ግንኙነት የሌላቸው ዝም ብለው የሚወረወሩ አረፍተ ነገሮች Premise ወይም Conclusion ስለማይሆኑ ይወገዳሉ።


📝 Exam-Style Practice Questions

Q1: Which of the following sentences can serve as a statement in a logical argument?
A) Please close the classroom door immediately.
B) How many students are enrolled in the Logic course?
C) Hawassa is the capital city of Sidama Region.
D) I suggest we take a short break now.
Answer: C
Explanation: A statement must have a truth-value (True or False). Option C is a declarative sentence that is True. A is a Command, B is a Question, and D is a Suggestion.

Q2: Identify the conclusion in the following argument: "Since taking care of health increases lifespan, and regular exercise improves health, it follows that regular exercise increases lifespan."
A) Taking care of health increases lifespan.
B) Regular exercise improves health.
C) Regular exercise increases lifespan.
D) Taking care of health is mandatory.
Answer: C
Explanation: The phrase "it follows that" is a Conclusion Indicator, making the statement immediately following it the conclusion.

Q3: Which of the following is TRUE regarding an argument in logic?
A) An argument can have multiple conclusions if there are multiple premises.
B) An argument must contain at least one premise and exactly one conclusion.
C) A bad argument is not considered an argument at all.
D) Any group of declarative sentences automatically forms an argument.
Answer: B
Explanation: By definition, an argument can have one or more premises, but it must contain one and only one conclusion.
